name: Cube frame (type file)
description: Hollow cube, open through every side
author: Boxsmith

params.label: Beam width
params.help: How wide each hollow edge beam is, outside to outside.

warnings.text: Beam width raised to {fmt(minW)} — the narrowest that leaves room for finger joints on both sides of each strip.
The beams are too wide for this size, so the openings would vanish. Beam width reduced to {fmt(w)}.
The box is too small for a cube frame in this material — make it bigger.

panel.name: Strip {k}{#k}
panel.at: axis(a)*(w - t) + axis(p)*(hp ? dims[p] - w : w - t) + axis(q)*(hq ? dims[q] : 0)

notes.text: Thirty parts: six outer rings (one per side) and 24 inner strips that line the tunnels. Each edge of the cube is a hollow square beam {fmt(w)} across.
Openings: {fmt(W-2*w)} × {fmt(H-2*w)} front and back, {fmt(D-2*w)} × {fmt(H-2*w)} on the sides, {fmt(W-2*w)} × {fmt(D-2*w)} top and bottom.

Strips come in four kinds (A–D) that differ only in their finger pattern. Build one beam at a time: glue the two inner strips into the bottom ring's opening, then add the side rings, then the top ring last.
Cube frame sizes are always outside dimensions.
Cube frames are glued; screw joints are turned off for this style.
